title: 8-Bit Player
description: herb's top songs converted into 8-bit chiptunes inside a pixel-crisp early-2000s player: each track's real 30-second preview is transcribed by a pitch model in the browser, split into melody, chords, bass and drums, and replayed on two pulse channels, a triangle and a noise kit. Drop in any song to convert it, save the result as MIDI, slide the EQ, drag the windows.
intent: One period object finished to the edge, now hearing the real songs: Spotify's Basic Pitch model runs in a worker on each track's preview, a beat tracker, chord Viterbi and line tracker turn its notes into parts, and the parts are rebuilt as an NES-style arrangement (band-limited pulse waves, tracker arpeggios, a stepped triangle, LFSR noise) on the song's own beat grid, so every readout on the skin is drawn from that signal.
sources: herb reference board: Y2K found-footage montage (fa23bcd4), CRT green terminal text and early-2000s media objects
